Zawichost Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zawichost, Poland

Not demolished. Zawichost absorbed the former town of Prosperów in 1820, where Jewish community development began in the 18th century; by 1921, 1,445 Jews (47.9%) were mostly murdered at Bełżec in October 1942. This cemetery, likely established in the first half of the 19th century, held roughly 200 ghetto liquidation victims from October 1942, though these bodies were reportedly exhumed and burned around 1944. German occupiers broke tombstones to gravel the road to Staszów during the war. Poland's local council voted to liquidate the cemetery in 1957, following provincial pressure; a 1963 resolution proposed single-family housing on the site, at which point authorities fenced the grounds, planted trees, and secured remaining bodies and monuments. The Minister of Municipal Economy issued final closure on June 26, 1964, with documentation noting the last burial occurred in 1942. Four separate plots were later carved from the original grounds.
